newsitem.title: USA: McDonald's 'on threshold' of value offer.
newsitem.headline: McDonald's 'on threshold' of value offer.

text.p: McDonald's Corp said Wednesday it plans to offer its customers what it called an "unprecedented value offering."
In a statement, McDonald's offered no details, except that it "will be good news for our customers and our franchisees and our business...but bad news for the competition."
A franchisee source, meanwhile, said McDonald's is planning a deep-discount promotion to jump-start customer traffic and sales at its outlets.

Dick Adams, chairman of the Consortium, an independent association of McDonald's franchisees, said the fast-food giant is planning a 12-month promotion that will feature a different sandwich priced at $0.55 each month when the order includes french fries and a drink.
He added that McDonald's is expected to present the plan in a satellite broadcast to operators across the country on Thursday.
"They (franchisees) are going to vote for it," Adams said. "They are being told that it's the only plan that is available."
The Wall Street Journal reported Wednesday that McDonald's plan, including the $0.55 price promotion, will be its biggest discounting program ever.
The newspaper, quoting an internal company document, said, "McDonald's pricing isn't competitive" and that cutting prices could reverse "the declining momentum of sales, transaction and cash flow."
The Wall Street Journal also said McDonald's strategy could "set off a price war of unprecedented proportions."
"The wild conclusions reached by The Wall Street Journal today are flat out wrong," McDonald's said in its statement.

"Conclusions about the state of our business, the price war and the conclusion about how this value-promotion will affect the business of our franchisees are all flat-out wrong," Jack Daly, vice president of McDonald's U.S. communications division, said in an interview.
